item.title: Trump's son 'opposed' Iran war, believed US should avoid another Middle East conflict
item.description: Donald Trump Jr expressed private opposition to the war with Iran, differing from his father's military approach. Despite sharing his views with close associates, he has avoided public disagreements with his father. The conflict has revealed divisions within the MAGA movement on foreign intervention. Domestic challenges, like rising fuel prices, have affected Trump's approval ratings amid the ongoing war.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Texas Ranch State Park Purchase: Foundation buys 650 acres for new park; phased opening from 2027
item.description: The Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation has acquired a family-run ranch in East Texas for future park development. This historic land, held by the Pollard family since 1940 and boasting valuable lakefront access, is set to transition to the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department by late 2027. The park will offer recreational opportunities while preserving the area’s ecological integrity, enabling the public to connect with nature.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Subway co-founder’s relative buys Connecticut warehouse for $6.75 million, plans renovation
item.description: A member of the Buck family has purchased a Danbury warehouse previously owned by the Salame family. This transaction, completed for $6.75 million, signals a commitment to modernizing the site while preserving its industrial purpose. Plans include extensive renovations and the construction of an office building alongside the warehouse. The investment reflects confidence in the local economy and aims to maintain vibrant commercial use of the property.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Cincinnati’s vacant Terrace Plaza Hotel faces fresh redevelopment hurdles over tax dispute
item.description: Cincinnati's iconic Terrace Plaza Hotel has stood vacant since 2008, currently tied up in redevelopment plans. A contentious property tax valuation dispute between the owner and the city's school district has caused delays. This $160 million project seeks to honor the hotel's historical significance while also requiring a resolution of tax issues to proceed with construction, maintaining its vital role in the city’s architectural legacy.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Sienna Miller’s £1.75m thatched cottage gets a £200k price cut
item.description: Sienna Miller's thatched cottage, known as Thatch, is currently listed for £1.75 million. The cottage, located in Buckinghamshire, offers a blend of historical charm and modern amenities. Originally purchased by Miller in 2008, it features four bedrooms and a stylish country kitchen. It embraces its 16th-century character while providing a peaceful rural lifestyle. The property is presented with a reduced asking price after being initially listed at £1.95 million.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Jeff Gordon’s foundation helped open Rwanda cancer centre; it treated 18,000+ patients by 2025
item.description: In 2012, Rwanda launched the Butaro Cancer Center of Excellence to fill the gap in cancer care services. Since then, it has treated over 18,000 individuals, greatly enhancing local healthcare. The center plays a crucial role by establishing vital diagnostic programs and training healthcare staff. However, challenges such as high drug costs and a lack of specialists remain, affecting survival rates.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida homeowners sue HOA, alleging a $232,000 roof deposit was paid before the public vote
item.description: Homeowners in The Vistas at Phillips Commons have initiated a lawsuit against their homeowners association. They allege that a roofing contract worth $2.1 million was approved secretly before an official vote. The residents claim that a significant deposit was made before the meeting took place, indicating potential financial misconduct. An active criminal investigation is examining alleged irregularities involving both the association and the management company.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Manhattan townhouse with 41-foot pool gets $1 million price cut
item.description: Nestled at 238 West 74th Street, this pristine townhouse dating back 140 years is available for $10.45 million. Spanning around 6,460 square feet, it boasts six bedrooms and six-and-a-half bathrooms. Unique features include a splendid 41-foot heated indoor pool and lush outdoor spaces, combining modern conveniences with historic charm. Its recent renovations enhance the classic aesthetics, and it has seen several price reductions from an initial $14.945 million.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Connecticut tenant wins $1.6 million after fall, but landlord's appeal leaves him unpaid
item.description: Michael Criscuolo, a resident of Connecticut, faced a life-changing injury after stumbling over construction debris near his apartment. A court ruled in his favor, granting him $1.6 million due to the landlord's clear negligence. Yet, Sim Levenhartz has failed to pay the awarded sum, with an appeal still in progress, prolonging Criscuolo's wait for justice. Meanwhile, the property deteriorates further, racking up municipal fines.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pennsylvania turned fire-damaged land bought for as little as 18 cents an acre into a million-tree park
item.description: Promised Land State Park in Pennsylvania originated from the acquisition of fire-damaged land between 1902 and 1904. Through dedicated efforts by the Civilian Conservation Corps, over a million trees were planted, transforming the landscape into a beautiful forested area. Recreation facilities were developed to enhance visitors' enjoyment, although the park faced hurdles like a tornado in 1998.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Eva Marcille faces $22,000 HOA lawsuit over unpaid fees and property violations at her Georgia home
item.description: Eva Marcille, known for her reality TV fame, is embroiled in a legal battle with her Georgia homeowners association due to claims of unpaid dues and property upkeep issues. The association alleges that Eva has failed to respond to multiple warnings concerning her property's state. Her attorney, Michael T. Sterling, has pledged to vigorously defend her, underscoring potential ramifications for homeowner rights in Georgia.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Man buys $30 drawing at estate sale, later linked to Renaissance master Dürer and valued at $10 million
item.description: A drawing bought for $30 at an estate sale in Massachusetts is confirmed to be by Albrecht Dürer. Experts attribute the ink sketch to 1503 and estimate its value between $10 million and $50 million. The anonymous buyer initially believed it to be a modern reproduction, showcasing his artistic instincts. Extensive analysis confirmed the drawing's authenticity and its links to Dürer’s other works.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Minnesota tribe reduces casino land request by nearly 75% after locals raise concerns
item.description: The White Earth Nation in Minnesota has reduced its proposed casino land-trust request from nearly 300 acres to 80 following concerns about drinking water, traffic, infrastructure costs, and property taxes. The project, planned for Clay County, has not yet received federal approval and also requires concurrence from Minnesota's governor. Tribal representatives say a decision could come by late 2028 under the most favourable circumstances.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 52-acre California vineyard once part of Hollywood star Fred MacMurray’s ranch lists for $22 million
item.description: Part of Hollywood actor Fred MacMurray’s 1,750-acre California ranch, the 52-acre Flax Estate and Vineyard in Healdsburg has hit the market for $22 million. Owned by philanthropists Jeffrey and Laurie Ubben, who bought the property for $21 million in 2016, the estate features 26 acres of organically farmed Pinot Noir vineyards and three residences.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: San Francisco co-op born after Black displacement gets $23 million boost for 2,400-home redevelopment
item.description: Freedom West Homes has acquired crucial funding to embark on an ambitious redevelopment initiative that will yield 2,400 new homes. This project prioritizes the needs of existing cooperative shareholders, ensuring they remain in place rather than face displacement. Notably, it focuses on replacing dilapidated structures while maintaining ownership for Black and immigrant families.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Australia’s endangered palm cockatoos get artificial nests; first chick fledges in world-first
item.description: A palm cockatoo chick has recently fledged from an artificial hollow in the Cape York Peninsula, marking a positive step for conservationists. They installed 29 artificial nesting hollows to combat the lack of natural breeding sites. This first successful breeding event is a pivotal achievement in palm cockatoo conservation. Ongoing monitoring will assess how well these new hollows can facilitate nesting and chick growth for this endangered species.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Glacier Cliffs Retreat And Stabilise: Study tracks rapid ice loss; long-term collapse less certain
item.description: Recent research reveals that Antarctica's glaciers are retreating at a faster pace than earlier predictions had estimated. By analyzing over 15,000 satellite images, scientists focused on the stability of ice cliffs. While some cliffs showed signs of quick retreat, they later stabilized instead of collapsing completely. Factors like water depth and the shape of the underlying bedrock significantly influence glacier stability.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
